newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end sharply down, outlook seen gloomy.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end sharply down, outlook seen gloomy.

text.p: Stocks closed sharply lower on Tuesday as President Kim Young-sam's press conference failed to ease jitters over the spreading labour strikes, brokers said.
The composite index ended at a provisional 611.05, down 2.52 percent or 15.82 points on the day. It once touched an intra-day low of 609.12.
Declining stocks overwhelmed gainers by 757 to 83. Trading volume totalled 24.07 million shares, up from Monday's 17.65 million.
"Investors dumped shares from disappointment at the conference that they had hoped would give a clue to resolving the labour crisis," said Koh Kyung-bae of Hyundai Securities.
"Prospects look even gloomier as the strikes will spread wider into more sectors of the economy."
President Kim backed a new labour law that has sparked nationwide strikes, saying it was needed to improve the nation's economic competitiveness.
More than 200,000 workers have joined the latest wave of industrial action, idling car plants and shipbuilding yards.
The new law, railroaded through parliament December 26 with only the ruling party members attending, allows employers to lay off workers, hire temporary staff and replace strikers.
But banking shares bucked the overall trend, benefitting from President Kim's remarks that he would establish a committee to speed up reform in the financial sector.
The industry's sub-index was up 1.28 percent to 395.91. Korea Exchange Bank rose 400 won to 8,000, KorAm Bank gained 510 won to 9,560 and Daedong Bank closed 140 won up to 4,450.
